title: Batch-window-aware KV quant sensitivity trials (FP8 / INT8 / INT4)
creator: Diego Morales
description:
Background:
We frequently hit GPU memory pressure on larger context workloads (>= 8k) when serving high-concurrency continuous batches. The KV cache dominates per-request memory in those cases. Previous investigations show that lower-bit encodings (FP8/INT8/INT4) can reduce resident memory but quality trade-offs and interaction with continuous batching windows are under-explored.

Goal:
Run a controlled matrix of quantization/compression trials for the KV cache that explicitly parameterize: compression format (FP8, symmetric INT8, asymmetric INT8, clustered INT4), batch-window duration (1ms, 5ms, 10ms), and cache placement rules (most-recent N tokens high-fidelity vs uniform low-fidelity). Measure quality regressions, latency tail behavior, and realized GPU memory savings in production-like continuous batching. Produce an automated decision guide for when to apply which profile and a prototype runtime switch for per-request fidelity selection.

Hypotheses:
- H1: FP8 will give ~30% memory reduction with negligible quality loss for short-context workloads and small batch windows (<=5ms).
- H2: INT8 (asymmetric) provides similar memory savings but sometimes introduces token-level logprob shifts that affect rare-token generation in long contexts.
- H3: INT4 yields highest memory reduction but causes measurable degradation on contextual coherence for requests that require deep KV lookups unless recent tokens are stored at higher fidelity.
- H4: Longer batch windows increase effective KV reuse and enable more aggressive quantization without proportional quality loss because cache hit patterns bias toward recent tokens.

Success criteria:
- Produce a recommendation matrix mapping workload archetypes -> quant profile with expected memory delta and worst-case quality delta (95th percentile).
- Implement a runtime feature-flagged prototype to change KV fidelity per-request and per-shard.
- End-to-end dashboards showing memory savings and customer-visible latency/quality trade-offs.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Models: rwd-13b, rwd-34b, and a Llama-2-13B baseline for cross-checking generality.
- Encodings: FP8 (e5-like), INT8 symmetric, INT8 asymmetric with per-channel scale, INT4 clustered (4-bit codebooks with per-shard lookup).
- Batch window: 1ms, 5ms, 10ms (continuous batching runtime knobs).
- Cache policies: recent-N high-fidelity (N=128,512), uniform low-fidelity, tiered (recent high, older compressed).
- Metrics: token-level KL to FP32 baseline, generation ROUGE-L on eval sets, human A/B for 200 prompts (synth+prod-like), 95/99 latency pcts, GPU resident memory, tail OOM/exception rates.

Data and evaluation sets:
- Synthetic long-context suite (prompt traces that exercise KV for long dependencies).
- Production-sampled prompt traces anonymized and filtered (privacy-checked) covering chat, summarization, code completion.
- Small human eval panel (internal) for coherence, factuality, and hallucination rate.

Instrumentation and telemetry:
- Add per-request fidelity tag to logs and traces.
- Track per-shard quant conversion error histogram and correlation with downstream token probability shifts.
- Dashboard: memory savings vs quality delta, and a bubble chart of batch-window vs quality regression.

Safety and rollback:
- Feature behind runtime gate and quota: only enabled for internal canaries and staging by default.
- Automatic fallback: if per-request generation entropy change > threshold or human-A/B shows >5% degrade, auto-fallback to FP32/FP16 cache for that cohort.

Deliverables:
- Experiment runbook and automation scripts (CI jobs to run full matrix overnight).
- Prototype runtime switch (feature-flag) for per-request KV fidelity selection + canary config.
- Public internal doc summarizing results and recommended default profiles.

Links to artifacts and infra:
See 'links' for PRs, confluence drafts, and Grafana panels.
updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created. Initial experiment matrix sketched; depend on runtime batch window metric hooks (ENG-771014).

2026-02-25: Landed lightweight FP8 encoder in bench harness; smoke-run on rwd-13b shows expected memory delta ~28% on 8k context. No runtime integration yet. (PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4129)

2026-03-02: Observed token-level KL drift concentrated on low-frequency tokens in synthetic long-context suite when using symmetric INT8. Created instrumentation to capture per-token logprob deltas. Added 'recent-N' policy test. (internal notebook: drive.redwood.com/kv-quant/notes)

2026-03-07: First continuous-batching run with 5ms window across rwd-13b with FP8 and INT8 asymmetric. Memory savings consistent; quality regression under 0.5% for automated metrics, but internal human checks flagged subtle coherence drops in code-completion prompts. Filed follow-up to test hybrid recent-N strategy.

2026-03-11: Prototype runtime flag added to staging cluster; canary traffic enabled for 10% of requests under the 'kv-quant' config. Dashboard skeleton created at grafana.redwood.com/d/kv-quant/2026-batch-window (PR for dashboard: github.com/redwood/observability/pull/278).

2026-03-14: Interim analysis: FP8 + recent-512 high-fidelity achieves ~26% mem reduction with <0.7% auto-metric regression and acceptable human A/B (n=120). INT4 still shows tail-case failures on long dependency prompts. Plan: expand human panel and run hybrid INT4-with-hotzone (recent tokens stored as 8-bit) next week.
